input.body:
label: bug
file: src/export/scheduler.ts

Thanks for the report. The scheduled-export logic in `nextRunAt`/`runDueExports` never looks at the recipient's account timezone at all — it always schedules and sends weekly reports at a single hard-coded UTC hour (`RUN_HOUR_UTC = 6`), and computes the "next Monday" purely by adding 7 UTC calendar days to the last UTC run date. That works out fine for accounts near UTC (e.g. London), but for an account far ahead of UTC (Sydney, UTC+10/+11) the same fixed UTC instant can fall on a different local calendar day/weekday than intended, so the weekly email that's supposed to land Monday morning locally slips to Tuesday. The fix should convert the recipient's configured timezone into the scheduling calculation (compute "next Monday 6am local" and convert that to UTC) instead of assuming all accounts share the same UTC delivery hour.

input.title: Fix scheduled export timing to respect recipient time zones
input.body: File: src/export/scheduler.ts. The scheduler computes nextRunAt using a fixed RUN_HOUR_UTC and weekly/monthly offsets purely in UTC, with no awareness of the report's or recipients' configured time zone. This means users far from UTC (e.g. Sydney, UTC+10/11) can have their "Monday morning" run land on Tuesday local time, while users closer to UTC (e.g. London) see the expected day. The fix should make nextRunAt (and/or runScheduledExport) take the report's configured time zone into account when computing the next scheduled run and the cutover day/hour, instead of assuming all recipients share the UTC calendar day.
